doc.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 23, 2003 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Four guitarists on a session: roles and overdubbing
summary: Each guitarist had a role such as rhythm, chinks or whole tones; sessions took as many passes as needed, with vocals sometimes overdubbed later.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: That makes me curious how, on a typical date with four guitar players, did you guys have roles that you kind of specialized in?

Yeah. One guy played rhythm, another guy did what they call “chinks” with the electric, real tight. Another guy went [scats], and another guy did whole tones with a Vibrolo [scats]. And after a while we could do it in our sleep. Now you do this and I’ll do that.
And how many passes did you usually get at a song?
As many as they needed. Sometimes the artist couldn’t get it so we did a lot of passes.
So if it got to that point we used to make a track and say come back tomorrow night and you can do it on your own.
So they did have overdubbing, as far as the vocal end of the thing.
